questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: In the context of Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates, what is the major organic product when 2-Methylcyclohexanone reacts under the following conditions: 1. LDA in THF, -78°C  2. CH₃I?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Bulky base LDA at -78°C abstracts the less hindered α-proton; subsequent alkylation yields the 2,6-isomer. The correct major product is '2,6-Dimethylcyclohexanone (Kinetic product)'.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: In the context of Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates, what is the major organic product when 2-Methylcyclohexanone reacts under the following conditions: 1. NaOEt in EtOH, 25°C  2. CH₃I?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Unhindered base under equilibrium conditions generates the more substituted, more stable enolate leading to 2,2-alkylation. The correct major product is '2,2-Dimethylcyclohexanone (Thermodynamic product)'.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: In the context of Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates, what is the major organic product when Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) reacts under the following conditions: cat. 0.1 M NaOH(aq) at 5°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Enolate of acetaldehyde attacks parent acetaldehyde at low temperature to yield the β-hydroxy aldehyde. The correct major product is '3-Hydroxybutanal (Aldol addition product)'.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: In the context of Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates, what is the major organic product when Acetaldehyde reacts under the following conditions: cat. 1.0 M NaOH(aq), 80°C (Δ)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Base-catalyzed E1cB dehydration of the aldol addition product upon heating yields the conjugated α,β-unsaturated enal. The correct major product is 'trans-2-Butenal (Crotonaldehyde) + H₂O'.

questions.chapter_title: Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates
questions.question: In the context of Alpha Carbon Chemistry: Enols and Enolates, what is the major organic product when Ethyl acetate (CH₃COOCH₂CH₃) reacts under the following conditions: 1. NaOEt (1.0 equiv), EtOH, reflux  2. H₃O⁺?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Enolate attacks parent ester in nucleophilic acyl substitution; final irreversible deprotonation drives equilibrium. The correct major product is 'Ethyl acetoacetate [CH₃COCH₂COOCH₂CH₃] + EtOH'.
